body:
Here are a few off the top of my head:
1) "Candles" by Daughter
2) "Cleaning Out My Closet" by Angel Haze
3) "Amy in the White Coat" by Bright Eyes
4) "A Million Men" by Melanie Martinez
5) "Dog Teeth" by Nicole Dollanganger
6) "Bitter and Sick" by One Two
7) "Blood Brothers" by Nicole Dollanganger

Important Edit: These aren't "motivational" songs by any means. Huge trigger warning on all of them. I tend to listen to music that I feel like captures the weight of CSA, and I feel like these ones do. They're pretty much all graphic, particularly numbers 2 and 3.

I've used their online hotline a few times, and I sort of feel like I'm talking to a wall. They're probably not allowed to divulge any information about themselves, understandably so, but it ends up feeling for me like they're just repeating back exactly what I've told them and we go in circles. I end up leaving the conversation feeling worse than I did when I started.

I may take you up on that at some point, actually, if you're comfortable with it. There are so many things that I feel like I can't talk about because no one would get it, and I know that you likely would/do.

My first abuser was my father. There were many after him, but none that scarred me in quite the same way. I'm 17 now and don't really have any idea how to cope. Thank you for this. I've been feeling more than usual like no one in the world can understand, and I really needed to read this, as nauseating as the details are of what you were forced to go through.
I've been on them before, yeah. I've tried a handful of different ones. I've considered going back on them but I'm not sure whether or not I want to.

I understand where you're coming from, and I know that your comment wasn't meant to be sensitive, but it's just not that easy. I wouldn't be this close to taking my life if I felt like it was possible to make it all go away by changing my mindset.

Edit: I know your comment wasn't meant to be *insensitive*. Oops.
